problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. Available containers are:

* Container 1: volume 38 m³, revenue $169
* Container 2: volume 21 m³, revenue $49
* Container 3: volume 46 m³, revenue $233
* Container 4: volume 22 m³, revenue $13
* Container 5: volume 7 m³, revenue $178
* Container 6: volume 38 m³, revenue $63
* Container 7: volume 36 m³, revenue $110
* Container 8: volume 37 m³, revenue $12
* Container 9: volume 2 m³, revenue $19
* Container 10: volume 20 m³, revenue $246
* Container 11: volume 8 m³, revenue $274
* Container 12: volume 43 m³, revenue $20
* Container 13: volume 32 m³, revenue $131
* Container 14: volume 18 m³, revenue $273
* Container 15: volume 20 m³, revenue $145
* Container 16: volume 13 m³, revenue $215
* Container 17: volume 39 m³, revenue $238
* Container 18: volume 31 m³, revenue $167
* Container 19: volume 22 m³, revenue $17
* Container 20: volume 49 m³, revenue $160
* Container 21: volume 7 m³, revenue $184
* Container 22: volume 45 m³, revenue $56
* Container 23: volume 10 m³, revenue $207

The vessel has a maximum cargo capacity of 422 m³. Choose the container combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully accepted or rejected.
